f.title: Use an alternative approach only if it satisfies applicable statutes and regulations
f.statement: An alternative approach to the one in this guidance can be used if the approach satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations; to discuss an alternative approach, contact the FDA staff responsible for implementing the guidance.
f.clause: Preamble (nonbinding statement)

f.title: Apply section 505(o)(4) safety labeling change provisions to non-marketed products unless approval is withdrawn
f.statement: The safety labeling changes provisions of section 505(o)(4) apply to prescription NDA products, BLA products, and ANDA products whose NDA RLD is not currently marketed, including products that are not marketed, unless approval of the NDA, BLA, or ANDA has been withdrawn in the Federal Register.

f.exceptions: Not applicable where approval of the NDA, BLA, or ANDA has been withdrawn in the Federal Register

f.statement: Application holders may submit labeling supplements for review at any time and without prior notification to FDA; such voluntary supplements are not addressed by this guidance.

f.title: Submit REMS document and material changes needed by required labeling changes as REMS modifications
f.statement: Where changes to prescribing information required under section 505(o)(4) necessitate changes to REMS documents and REMS materials, these changes should be submitted as REMS modifications pursuant to section 505-1 of the FD&C Act.

f.title: Make safety labeling changes required in an FDA notification letter
f.statement: A holder of an approved NDA, BLA, or ANDA without a marketed NDA reference listed drug (RLD) will be notified and required to make the safety labeling changes, unless approval of the application has been formally withdrawn in a Federal Register notice.

f.title: Comply with notification letter requirements for discontinued products unless approval is withdrawn
f.statement: Requirements under section 505(o)(4) apply to NDAs, BLAs, and ANDAs without a currently marketed RLD approved under an NDA, including discontinued products, unless approval of the application has been withdrawn in the Federal Register; therefore requirements described in a safety labeling change notification letter apply unless approval has been withdrawn in the Federal Register.

f.title: Distribute product with CBE-0 changes upon FDA receipt of the supplement
f.statement: A changes-being-effected (CBE-0) supplement proposes changes that do not require FDA approval prior to distribution; for such changes the application holder may distribute the product with the changes upon FDA's receipt of the supplement (21 CFR 314.70(c)(6) and 601.12(f)(2)).

f.title: Respond to a notification letter with a labeling supplement or a rebuttal statement
f.statement: After receiving notification of required safety labeling changes, the application holder must either submit a supplement with proposed labeling changes to reflect the new safety information, or notify FDA that it does not believe a labeling change is warranted and submit a statement detailing the reasons why such a change is not warranted (a rebuttal statement).
f.clause: IV.B. How Should Application Holders Respond to a Notification Letter?

f.statement: In FDA's view, the labeling changes process under 21 CFR 314.70 and 601.12 continues to apply to application holders when the application holder becomes aware of newly acquired information, including in circumstances that meet the criteria for submission of a supplement - changes-being-effected (CBE-0).

f.title: Revise prescription drug labeling to warn of a clinically significant hazard on reasonable evidence of causal association
f.statement: To implement the statutory prohibition against marketing a misbranded product, 21 CFR 201.57(c)(6) requires that prescription drug labeling be revised to include a warning about a clinically significant hazard as soon as there is reasonable evidence of a causal association with a drug (see also FD&C Act sections 502(a), (f), (j), and (n)).

f.applicability: Prescription drug labeling

f.title: Recognise limits on ANDA labeling changes through CBE supplements
f.statement: Because an ANDA's labeling must be the same as the NDA RLD's labeling (with exceptions in 21 CFR 314.94(a)(8)(iv)), ANDA holders cannot make labeling changes through the formal supplement process under 21 CFR 314.70 in all circumstances in which NDA holders can; the changes-being-effected process under 21 CFR 314.70(c) is not expressly available to ANDA holders except to match the RLD labeling or to respond to FDA's specific request to submit a labeling change under this provision.
f.clause: IV.B. (footnote 10)
f.applicability: ANDA labeling
f.exceptions: Except to match the RLD labeling or to respond to FDA's specific request to submit a labeling change; exceptions to sameness in 21 CFR 314.94(a)(8)(iv)

rows.quote: Under existing FDA regulations, ANDA holders cannot make labeling changes through the formal supplement process under 21 CFR 314.70 in all circumstances in which NDA holders can because an ANDA’s labeling must be the same as the NDA RLD’s labeling (with some exceptions, as described in 21 CFR 314.94(a)(8)(iv)). Accordingly, the changes-being-effected supplement process under 21 CFR 314.70(c) is not expressly available to ANDA holders except to match the RLD labeling or to respond to FDA’s specific request to submit a labeling change under this provision.

f.title: Meet ANDA postmarketing adverse event reporting, procedure and annual reporting duties
f.statement: ANDA holders have a duty to inform FDA of certain adverse events in compliance with postmarket reporting requirements, to develop written procedures for the surveillance, receipt, evaluation, and reporting of postmarket adverse drug experiences, and to annually report information that might affect the safety, effectiveness, or labeling of the drug product (21 CFR 314.80, 314.81, and 314.98).

f.title: Submit the labeling supplement or rebuttal statement within 30 calendar days of the notification letter
f.statement: Following notification, the labeling supplement or rebuttal statement must be submitted within 30 days (section 505(o)(4)(B)); FDA interprets this as within 30 calendar days of the date the notification letter is issued.

f.title: FDA to inform all class application holders when a discussion period is initiated on alternative wording
f.statement: If the notification letter was issued for more than one application and one or more holders submit language differing from the notification letter, FDA will inform all holders that received a notification letter that a discussion period will be initiated; the period begins on the date FDA receives the submission and lasts no more than 30 calendar days unless an extension is warranted.

f.title: FDA to approve or order labeling within 15 calendar days after the discussion period on a supplement
f.statement: Within 15 calendar days of the conclusion of the 30-day discussion period (and any extension), FDA will send a supplement approval letter if consensus is reached; if FDA does not agree with the proposed changes and no consensus is reached, FDA can order the application holder to make the required labeling changes under section 505(o)(4)(E).

f.title: FDA may extend the discussion period and notify the holder in writing before it ends
f.statement: Under section 505(o)(4)(D), FDA may extend the discussion period beyond 30 days if it determines an extension is warranted (usually for another 30 days, e.g. drug class changes or significantly revised language); before the discussion period concludes, FDA may notify the application holder in writing that it has been extended and, when possible, briefly state the reasons.

FDA expects that an extension of the discussion period (usually for another 30 days) will be warranted when a 30-day discussion period may not suffice to adequately address all outstanding issues (e.g., the labeling change involves a drug class or the supplement contains significantly revised language). In such cases, before the conclusion of the discussion period, FDA may notify the application holder in writing that the 30-day discussion period has been extended and, when possible, briefly state the reason(s) for the extension.
